result.topic_en: Series expansion of the arithmetic-geometric mean M(1+x,1-x) via the substitution x = 2t/(1+tt). The page finds by induction that the coefficients of 1/M(1+x,1-x) are squares of the products (1·3·5…)/(2·4·6…), then begins article 7 to treat the reciprocal series directly.
result.transcription:
10
endo $M(1+x,1-x) = 1 + \alpha xx + \beta x^4 + \gamma x^6 + \delta x^8 + \text{etc.}$ (nam potestates ipsius $x$ cum exponente impari non adesse sponte patet):
habebitur
$(1+tt)\left(1+\alpha\left(\frac{2t}{1+tt}\right)^2 + \beta\left(\frac{2t}{1+tt}\right)^4 + \gamma\left(\frac{2t}{1+tt}\right)^6 + \delta\left(\frac{2t}{1+tt}\right)^8 + \text{etc.}\right) =$
$1 + \alpha t^4 + \beta t^8 + \gamma t^{12} + \delta t^{16} + \text{etc.}$

Hinc prodeunt aequationes
$1+4\alpha = 0$
$-4\alpha + 16\beta = \alpha$
$4\alpha - 48\beta + 64\gamma = 0$
$-4\alpha + 96\beta - 320\gamma + 256\delta = \beta$
etc.
vnde
$\alpha = -\frac{1}{4}$
$\beta = -\frac{5}{64}$
$\gamma = -\frac{11}{256}$
$\delta = -\frac{29}{1024} - \frac{5}{16384} = -\frac{469}{16384}$
etc.

In hac quoque serie coëfficientes legi simplici non subiecti sunt: at si vnitas per illam seriem diuiditur, prodit
$\frac{1}{M(1+x,1-x)} = 1 + \frac{1}{4}xx + \frac{9}{64}x^4 + \frac{25}{256}x^6 + \frac{1225}{16384}x^8 + \text{etc.}$
vbi primo aspectu videmus, [-omnes-] coëfficientes esse quadrata radicum $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{3}{4}$, $\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{3}{4}\cdot\frac{5}{6}$, $\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{3}{4}\cdot\frac{5}{6}\cdot\frac{7}{8}$, adeoque secundum legem persimplicem progredi. Sed methodus, per quam ad hanc conclusionem pulcherrimam peruenimus, inductionis tantummodo vim habet; quam ad certitudinis gradum euehere in disquisitionibus sqq. nobis proponimus.
7. Supponendo $\frac{1}{M(1+x,1-x)} = 1 + Axx + Bx^4 + Cx^6 + \text{etc.}$
atque vt in art. praec. $x = \frac{2t}{1+tt}$ habemus
$1 + A\left(\frac{2t}{1+tt}\right)^2 + B\left(\frac{2t}{1+tt}\right)^4 + C\left(\frac{2t}{1+tt}\right)^6 + D\left(\frac{2t}{1+tt}\right)^8 + \text{etc.} =$
$1 + tt + At^4 + At^6 + Bt^8 + Bt^{10} + Ct^{12} + Ct^{14} + Dt^{16} + Dt^{18} + \text{etc.}$

items.english: for it is self-evident that powers of x with odd exponent are not present

items.quote: vbi primo aspectu videmus, [-omnes-] coëfficientes esse quadrata radicum $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{3}{4}$, $\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{3}{4}\cdot\frac{5}{6}$, $\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{3}{4}\cdot\frac{5}{6}\cdot\frac{7}{8}$, adeoque secundum legem persimplicem progredi.
items.english: where at first sight we see that the coefficients are squares of the roots 1/2, 1/2·3/4, 1/2·3/4·5/6, 1/2·3/4·5/6·7/8, and thus proceed according to a very simple law.

items.quote: Sed methodus, per quam ad hanc conclusionem pulcherrimam peruenimus, inductionis tantummodo vim habet; quam ad certitudinis gradum euehere in disquisitionibus sqq. nobis proponimus.
items.english: But the method by which we arrived at this most beautiful conclusion has only the force of induction; we propose to raise it to the level of certainty in the following investigations.
